digest.component_or_area: completion-verification gate, LLM agent tool loop guard
propositions: The runaway guard layer sits outermost and counts memo-served (free) repeated file reads as loop evidence before the memo layer can answer them, causing the ratio arm to trip despite the memoization layer making those repeats cost-free.

The guard and memo layers compose with conflicting semantics: lever 2 (memo caching) makes repeats cheap and harmless, but the outermost guard punishes all distinct calls in its window without distinguishing executed work from cache-served results.

Completion verification runs fail with RunawayToolLoopError when the verifier re-reads memoized evidence files, blocking legitimate ticket closes despite earlier fixes, forcing authors toward --force flag.

The fix recomposes guard and memo via a shared ToolCallLedger that tracks executed vs observed calls; the memo records execution only at five concrete sites (passthrough, cache miss, uncached fallback, etc.), allowing the guard's ratio arm to evaluate only the executed stream while a served-streak backstop bounds pure cache-served loops.

Cache-served repeats no longer generate loop evidence for the distinct-ratio arm since they are not recorded as executed work; only genuine tool invocations increment the execution stream that the ratio checks.
